entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:1
segments: ¶THE BELOVED How beautiful are your feet in sandals, O prince's daughter! The curves of your thighs [are] like jewels, The work of the hands of a skillful workman.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:2
segments: Your navel [is] a rounded goblet; It lacks no blended beverage. Your waist [is] a heap of wheat Set about with lilies.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:3
segments: Your two breasts [are] like two fawns, Twins of a gazelle.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:4
segments: Your neck [is] like an ivory tower, Your eyes [like] the pools in Heshbon By the gate of Bath Rabbim. Your nose [is] like the tower of Lebanon Which looks toward Damascus.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:5
segments: Your head [crowns] you like [Mount] Carmel, And the hair of your head [is] like purple; A king [is] held captive by [your] tresses.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:6
segments: How fair and how pleasant you are, O love, with your delights!

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:7
segments: This stature of yours is like a palm tree, And your breasts [like] its clusters.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:8
segments: I said, "I will go up to the palm tree, I will take hold of its branches." Let now your breasts be like clusters of the vine, The fragrance of your breath like apples,

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:9
segments: And the roof of your mouth like the best wine. THE SHULAMITE [The wine] goes [down] smoothly for my beloved, Moving gently the lips of sleepers.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:10
segments: ¶I [am] my beloved's, And his desire [is] toward me.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:11
segments: Come, my beloved, Let us go forth to the field; Let us lodge in the villages.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:12
segments: Let us get up early to the vineyards; Let us see if the vine has budded, [Whether] the grape blossoms are open, [And] the pomegranates are in bloom. There I will give you my love.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 7:13
segments: The mandrakes give off a fragrance, And at our gates [are] pleasant [fruits], All manner, new and old, Which I have laid up for you, my beloved.
